Subject: New vendor onboarding — Aurora Systems (banking info + PO)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking us on as a vendor — excited to get this moving. I attached our standard vendor profile and an ACH template; please let me know which fields you need filled to get a PO created and how you prefer to receive invoices/remittance emails. A few specifics from our side:

- First invoice will be for onboarding fee (one-time) and will reference a contract number we’ll provide.
- For the ongoing monthly invoice we can do ACH or wire; ACH is preferred but we sometimes require a wire for the initial setup.
- Our standard payment terms are Net-30, but we can discuss Net-45 for larger enterprise discounts.

Attachments: aurora_vendor_profile.xlsx (vendor profile), aurora_ach_template.pdf (banking fields), aurora_initial-invoice-sample.pdf

Could you confirm:
1) Redwood’s remit-to email address for automated remittance?
2) PO number timing — will you issue a PO before the first invoice?
3) Any additional forms (W-9, tax docs) required on your side?

Thanks — looking to finalize bank details today so treasury can approve the ACH.

Best,
Anika Gupta

Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — Aurora Systems (banking info + PO)

Hi Anika — great to meet you. Thanks for the attachments, that helps. A few quick items so we can get the finance/onboarding teams moving:

- Remit-to: Accounts Payable prefers invoices to be sent to ap-invoices@redwood.com (PDF) and a separate remittance email to ap-remit@redwood.com with payment details. If you can include the PO number in the invoice subject/body that speeds reconciliation.
- PO timing: We usually create a PO once the vendor profile and W-9 are on file. Standard turnaround is 2 business days after we have completed docs.
- Forms: Please attach a completed W-9 (for US entities) or W-8 if applicable. Our procurement intake also asks for a billing contact and a remittance contact — those can be the same.
- ACH vs wire: Finance (cc’d) will review the ACH template. For first invoices we sometimes require a signed ACH authorization and may process the first payment via wire if Treasury requests additional verification.

Ben — can you confirm whether Treasury will require a notarized ACH form for first-time vendors or if the template + voided check is sufficient? Lauren — can you flag this in the onboarding checklist so the PO isn’t created until we confirm bank credentials?

I’ll follow up once we have Treasury’s guidance.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — Aurora Systems (banking info + PO)

Mina — quick note: Treasury prefers the ACH template + one of the following for new vendors:
1) Voided company check, or
2) Bank letter on bank letterhead confirming account and routing, or
3) DocuSign-signed ACH authorization (our standard).

For higher-risk vendors we ask for a micro-deposit verification; for trusted partners the template + voided check is usually enough. If Aurora prefers a wire for the setup payment, we’ll accept that but need wire instructions (beneficiary name, account, routing, SWIFT if international).

I’ll approve once we have either the voided check or the DocuSign completed. Please also attach the W-9.

—Ben
Ben Carter
